chunks: But they were seized by the mighty blast towards the morning;

key_terms.الصَّيْحَةُ: The mighty blast or loud cry that destroys the people
key_terms.مُصْبِحِينَ: In the morning, specifically early morning

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'as-sayhah' refer to in the context of divine punishment in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the destruction of the people of Lot, illustrating how divine retribution strikes when the appointed time arrives, catching the arrogant off guard. The 'morning' (musbihin) signifies the dawn of their ruin, serving as a warning for believers to remain vigilant against spiritual complacency. This event underscores the inevitability of God's decree and the suddenness with which worldly power can be overturned.
